issue: 'dh₃éntu h₁ésmey téwe bʰoh₂góm' for 'Give him your portion': dh₃éntu is the 3pl imperative 'let them give', but the addressee is 2sg (the preceding ph₃dʰí, mē dʰrugʰyés). It needs dh₃dʰí, which the packet uses elsewhere (a193a252, 55f7efb5, 88c1bd30). The rest is good, including dusḱléwēs (cf. Gk δυσκλεής) and ḱóm + instrumental ḱéywoh₁ 'with a friend'.

This is Lühr (2008), sentence 1, faithfully transcribed. The problems are notation and ablaut only. h₂wlh₂néh₂ has h₂ where the lexicon and most handbooks have *h₂wl̥h₁néh₂ (lexicon h₂wĺ̥h₁neh₂), and the syllabic l is unmarked. The syllabic m is unmarked in wéǵʰontm, méǵoh₂m and dʰǵʰémonm (for -m̥). gʷérh₂um has full grade against the project's gʷr̥h₂ús (Ved. gurú-). Parenthesised (H), (h₁) segments clash with the corpus notation. The syntax and the sense ('on which there was no wool … one … one … one') are right.
ph₂ter is an accentless vocative, a documented representation limitation (STATUS, Known limitations 2).

Byrd's King and the God, line 9, faithfully transcribed. súHnum has the accent on the root against the lexicon's suHnúm (Ved. sūnúm). wēlh₁mi is accentless because Byrd follows the Vedic rule that main-clause verbs are unaccented, which the project does not use: a Narten *wḗlh₁mi is expected. As a single line of dialogue it is an excerpt, not a truncated text.
ph₂ter is an accentless vocative, a documented limitation. mérs 'you died' is an active root aorist, which is the accepted t021 convention for mért.

'téwe bʰréh₂term̥ mē linkʷtóm': the verb is correctly 2du, addressed to the two sons, but the possessor téwe 'of you (sg.)' is singular. The reflexive possessive swóm 'your own' would avoid the clash; the engine has no 2du genitive. Otherwise the duals are exemplary: súHnuh₁, ḱlutóm, dwóh₁ bʰréh₂terh₁e steh₂róh₁, h₁édtom, píph₃etom.

méǵh₂ih₂ (fem. nom. sg.) has the accent on the root. Ved. mahī́ points to a suffix-accented *meǵh₂íh₂ (the devī type). The text is otherwise good: the correlatives h₁yós … h₁ím, dedórḱe 'sees', and Perkunos striking the oath-breaker.

'yugóy stesth₂é uh₃wé-kʷe …' for 'You two stand at the yoke': stesth₂é is the 2pl perfect. The rest of the text addresses the two horses consistently in the dual (uh₃wé, HéHḱuh₁ h₁éḱwoh₁, h₂isḱétes, h₁édtes), so this is a number mismatch. The engine has no PRF.2DU cell. The present sth₂éh₁yetes (2du) is available.
gʷh₂te is an accentless vocative, a documented representation exception. The accusative of goal wĺ̥kʷom with h₁éytu 'go to the wolf' is acceptable.
'ḱwṓ toy sédyetes HréwdHti-kʷe' for 'Your dog sits and cries': sédyetes is 2/3du, but the subject ḱwṓ is singular, and the coordinated HréwdHti is 3sg. It needs sédyeti.

Note on punctuation: 'gʷʰr̥nós bʰéwgtu swidyétu.' puts 'let him sweat' in the sentence about the warm, while the English starts a new sentence there. The forms are fine, including mē + optative trésoyh₁t as a negative wish.

ph₂ter is an accentless vocative, a documented limitation. h₁rudʰéh₁n̥t is the neuter participle 'red', homographic with the 3pl injunctive. h₁rudʰrós would be the plainer adjective, but the participle is acceptable.

'gʰóstis dh₃tr̥bʰós memóne' for 'The guest remembers the giver': dh₃tr̥bʰós is dat./abl. plural. 'Remember' takes an accusative or genitive object, and the English is singular. It needs déh₃torm̥, as in 55f7efb5.

kúdʰe 'where' has the plain velar from the Wiktionary headword. That goes against the project's boukólos convention, which keeps kʷ before syllabic u and lists M&A kʷu 'where' (*kʷúdʰe). gʷā́m (1sg aorist) writes the Stang outcome of *gʷéh₂m̥ beside gʷéh₂s in the same text (cf. t021 ḱlḗm). As in t021, h₁íns is masc. for gʷṓs. The question-and-answer form and ń̥dʰgʷʰitom ḱléwos are excellent.

'ne ǵorh₂éyeth₂e' for 'you did not grow old' uses the middle of the causative 'make old'. The intransitive *ǵérh₂- (Ved. járati, jīryati) is the plain choice. 'h₁rudʰéh₁n̥t kréwh₂s h₂éǵroy h₁ésti' says 'red blood is on the field' and drops the English 'your' (toy). It also repeats 'in the field' from the previous English sentence, which the PIE does not render.

The English has six sentences and the PIE five: the last sentence, 'Dawn follows the night', has no PIE counterpart. This is an omitted sentence, not a grammar error, so the pair does not say the same thing. Also minor: pl̥h₁éwih₂n̥s (fem. acc. pl. 'many') has a full-grade, accented suffix where Ved. purvī́ḥ points to *pl̥h₁wíh₂n̥s.

Byrd (2013), sentence 3, faithfully transcribed (u̯ → w). The problems are notation only. Byrd's a-colouring spelling (h₂áwyes, h₂wl̥h₁náh₂) differs from the corpus's h₂wĺ̥h₁neh₂. agʰnutór lacks the initial h₂ of *h₂egʰ-. h₁esti is unaccented following Byrd's Vedic main-clause rule. The English 'the sheep has' is singular, but h₂áwibʰyos is plural. wept 'wove' (*webʰ-) for 'makes' is Byrd's choice. The closing quotation mark is missing.

'ph₂wénbʰos úd h₁éyti' for 'fire goes up': ph₂wénbʰos is dat./abl. plural, but the subject needs the nominative péh₂wr̥, as in the next sentence. As written it says '(it) goes up from/for the fires'. The rest is good, including the neuter dual ḱéywoyh₁ with coordinated péh₂wr̥ wódr̥-kʷe.

'kʷŕ̥mey h₁yós h₁ésh₂r̥ píph₃esi n̥ḱéntu' for 'Worm, you who drink the blood, vanish!': n̥ḱéntu is the 3pl imperative 'let them vanish', but the addressee is the singular worm (2sg píph₃esi, parallel to mr̥dʰí). It needs the 2sg imperative n̥ḱdʰí.
